lines.text: [curious] Arjun... close your eyes for a second.
[laughs softly] Okay. They're closed.
Now tell me... which side is red?
[short pause] Hmm... [sighs] I can't. Without my eyes, it's just... plastic.
[thoughtful] One in twelve boys sees colour differently. And some kids can't see colour at all. The world's favourite puzzle... was only ever made for eyes.
[curious] So what if the colours... could be felt?
[warmly] That's the LVC Dream Cube. Every colour gets its own texture. White is smooth. Green has a raised frame. Orange... ridges.
[surprised] Wait, these are rings. So this is... red?
[laughs] Red. Blue is dots. And yellow is...
[excited] The big dome! I found it without looking!
Now a child who mixes up red and green never has to guess again. And blind and low-vision kids can solve it by touch... right next to their friends.
[thoughtful] And for the rest of us?
[softly] Lights off. Phone down. Just you, the cube and your fingertips... before sleep.
[whispers] A puzzle... in the dark.
Right now it's a prototype. 3D-printed chips, glued onto an ordinary cube. It works... but it isn't ready yet.
So that's where backers come in.
[earnestly] Yes. We'll test it with the kids it's meant for, make durable moulded chips, and add braille and audio instructions.
And schools and NGOs get it for under ten dollars a cube.
Twenty-four ninety-nine for you... and every cube helps put one in a classroom.
[curious] And the design files?
Free. Open source. For everyone.
[short pause] [thoughtful] So one small change... and a toy made for eyes becomes a toy made for everyone.
[warmly] LVC Dream Cube. See it. Feel it. Solve it.
[excited] Back us on Kickstarter.
